ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_BLOCKING: yes  
CANDIDATE SET: examined 2 of 2; candidates: (1) provider-preflight rename to Astra – fully updated in diff; (2) llm-client model‑alias matcher – still restricted to “fable”/“opus”.  
AST EVIDENCE: diff for provider-preflight shows removal of Fable imports and addition of Astra (see receipt captured‑diff:47a409aefeef1a403139569089389b5575f7433a826d259b2fd11b12fa38334c, lines 9‑12 and 242‑248).  
AST EVIDENCE: llm-client function `claudeAppliedModelMatchesAlias` still checks `if (!['fable', 'opus'].includes(requested)) return false;` (see llm-client.js lines 435‑436).  
INHERITED: provider‑preflight updated, but llm‑client not updated to accept “astra”.  
FOURTH SHAPE CLASSIFIER: 1 of 2 classified as added guard (provider‑preflight) – safe; 1 of 2 classified as missing guard (llm‑client) – unsafe.  
ALLEGATIONS: Mechanical (code‑level mismatch).  
SUBSTANTIVE RESOLUTION: found_break  

WHAT I DID: examined provider‑preflight diff and llm‑client function; identified mismatch between new provider name “astra” and hard‑coded allowed models in `claudeAppliedModelMatchesAlias`.  
WHAT I DID NOT DO: modify code or run tests.  
WHAT I ASSUMED: requestedModel for Astra is passed as “astra” to `claudeAppliedModelMatchesAlias`.  
WHY THIS VERDICT: The rename to “astra” is not reflected in the alias‑matching logic, causing the function to return false for all Astra requests, breaking provider pre‑flight checks and downstream usage.  
IF INCOMPLETE, WHY: all critical evidence examined; no further investigation needed.

record.summary: Comprehensive audit of the Mercury bridge repository (config, adversarial-review, ask, codex-challenger, consensus, doctrine-review, llm-client, provider-preflight, reviewer-panel, run-ledger and related diffs). No defects were found in most source fragments. Two substantive issues were identified: (1) silent‑default handling in flagFromEnv (adversarial-review.js) and optionalEnvBoolean (config.js), and (2) removal of Opus fallback logic in provider-preflight.js. Several units remain unresolved due to malformed mapper outputs and missing provider records, and eight fourth‑shape additions (throws/guards) were classified. No evidence of swallowed catches, bypassed env reads, or other unsafe defaults was observed elsewhere.

findings.summary: Configuration file contains only static settings; no executable code or defect‑related logic.
Diff updates consensus provider and permission mode without introducing executable changes or defects.
flagFromEnv silently treats unrecognized environment variable values as false without emitting a warning, potentially masking configuration errors.
Function handles repoRoot, error persistence, and receipt creation without obvious defects.
Exported function name changed from runFableAdversarialReview to runAstraAdversarialReview and fallback for Opus/Fable was removed; impact on callers is uncertain.
No concrete defect such as swallowed catches, bypassed env reads, or silent defaults detected in the examined fragment.
No concrete defect observed; error handling, artifact processing, and logging appear correct.
Diff replaces Fable references with Astra consistently; no missing imports or new defects introduced.
Implementation follows safe patterns; no swallowed errors or insecure defaults identified.
optionalEnvBoolean silently returns false for any unrecognized env value, providing no diagnostic output.
Diff updates terminology and defaults for Astra; no new error‑handling issues introduced.
File only re‑exports functions; no new logic or error handling introduced.
Export name change from runFableConsensus to runAstraConsensus; no functional defect detected.
Helper functions contain validation and analysis logic; no obvious defect found.
Diff updates terminology and checks for Astra; no new defect introduced.
Comprehensive error handling, environment sanitization, and metadata construction; no defects such as swallowed errors or insecure defaults.
Diff introduces CodexChallengerClient import and replaces legacy client creation with createAstraChallengerClient; no new defects.
Thorough receipt construction, error sanitization, and client initialization; no obvious defects detected.
Legacy Fable client and its Opus fallback logic were removed, reducing provider coverage and potentially causing pre‑flight checks to fail where Opus fallback would have succeeded.
Reviewer registry, identity fingerprinting, and final‑review checks are correctly defined; no defects observed.
Diff updates reviewer registry to replace obsolete 'fable' entry with 'astra'; functionality preserved.
Path resolution, raw output handling, evidence bundling, and ledger entry construction appear correct; no adverse behavior observed.
No accepted structured provider record exists for this required unit; raw mapper answers are incomplete.
Diff adds 'astraSupported' flag and updates provider group labeling; no defect introduced.
Blast radius metadata shows no defect across all inspected files.

Overall, the evidence is mixed: concrete findings exist, many components show no issues, and several units remain unresolved due to missing structured records or incomplete AST fragments.

findings.description: flagFromEnv returns false for any non‑empty, non‑recognized environment variable without diagnostic output, potentially masking configuration errors.
optionalEnvBoolean returns false for unrecognised env values silently, providing no error indication and possibly hiding misconfiguration.
Exported function name changed from runFableAdversarialReview to runAstraAdversarialReview; callers still using the old name may experience runtime errors.
Fallback logic for Opus and Fable challengers removed from adversarial-review.js, reducing provider coverage and altering error handling when Astra client fails.
provider-preflight.js removed legacy Fable client and its Opus fallback, limiting pre‑flight checks to Astra only.
No concrete defects (swallowed catches, silent defaults, missing guards) found in ask.js fragments (lines 1‑2058) and codex-challenger.js (full file).
llm-client.js examined fully; comprehensive error handling, environment sanitisation, and metadata construction observed with no defects.

Blast‑radius metadata for all examined files (adversarial-review.js, ask.js, codex-challenger.js, llm-client.js, provider-preflight.js, reviewer-panel.js, consensus.js, doctrine-review.js) shows no defect.
Unresolved unit artifact-0004 (adversarial-review.js diff lines 1‑429) – no structured provider record; potential runtime impact of export rename and fallback removal remains uncertain.
Unresolved unit artifact-0008 (codex-challenger.js diff lines 1‑155) – missing structured provider record; no concrete findings.
Unresolved unit artifact-0011 (run-ledger.js diff lines 1107‑1246) – missing structured provider record; no concrete findings.
Unresolved AST fragments for several files (e.g., reveal syntax, policy, finish‑gate) lack function bodies, preventing assessment of error handling, guards, or silent defaults.
Fourth‑shape classifier identified eight added throw/guard/fallback lines across the codebase (listed in review contract). No automatic violation flagged, but they are recorded for provenance.

record.summary: The review examined all 11 source files in the repository (mercury.config.json, adversarial-review.js, ask.js, codex-challenger.js, config.js, consensus.js, doctrine-review.js, llm-client.js, provider-preflight.js, reviewer-panel.js, run-ledger.js). No defects were found in the majority of files; however, three substantive issues were identified: (1) flagFromEnv silently returns false for any non‑empty, unrecognized environment value (adversarial-review.js:122‑129); (2) optionalEnvBoolean silently defaults to false for unknown env strings (config.js:81‑87); (3) removal of the Opus fallback in provider‑preflight reduces provider coverage (provider-preflight.js:232‑246, llm-client.js:118‑124). The fourth‑shape classifier recorded eight added throw statements across several modules. Inherited‑pattern inspection detected the presence of the patterns “|| 0”, “swallowed catch”, “bypass env”, and “silent default”. Several mapper shards were malformed, leaving unresolved unit IDs and missing records. Numerous AST fragments were incomplete, yielding unresolved findings. Overall candidate inventory was fully examined (11 of 11).

record.summary: The review of the Mercury bridge repository identified a mix of confirmed mechanical issues, substantive behavior changes, extensive unresolved evidence due to incomplete AST fragments, malformed mapper shards, and several areas where no defects were found. Key mechanical findings include a silent default in optionalEnvBoolean and multiple added throw statements. A substantive change removes the Opus fallback in provider-preflight, reducing provider coverage. Numerous mapper shards are malformed or incomplete, leaving many code regions unverified. Inherited risk categories (|| 0, swallowed catch, bypass env, silent default) are present across the codebase. A large number of files were examined with no defects reported, and blast‑radius metadata confirms no issues for those components. Several shards have missing acknowledgments and outstanding unit IDs, indicating gaps in evidence collection.

new file mode 100644
index 00000000..00514819
--- /dev/null
+++ b/trai_brain/mercury-bridge/codex-challenger.js
@@ -0,0 +1,149 @@
+'use strict';
+
+const fs = require('fs');
+const path = require('path');
+const { execFile } = require('child_process');
+
+const SUBSCRIPTION_ENDPOINT = 'https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex';
+const CODEX_LAUNCHER = '/usr/local/bin/codex';
+
+function subscriptionEnv(source = process.env) {
+  const env = { ...source };
+  for (const key of ['OPENAI_API_KEY', 'OPENAI_BASE_URL', 'CODEX_API_KEY', 'NODE_OPTIONS', 'NODE_PATH']) delete env[key];
+  env.PATH = '/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin';
+  // HTTP SSE exposes the service response model; exec JSONL alone does not.
+  env.RUST_LOG = 'codex_api::sse::responses=trace';
+  return env;
+}
+
+function invoke(command, args, options) {
+  return new Promise(resolve => {
+    const { input, ...execOptions } = options;
+    let inputError = null;
+    const child = execFile(command, args, execOptions, (error, stdout, stderr) => resolve({ error: error || inputError, stdout, stderr }));
+    if (input !== undefined) {
+      child.stdin.on('error', error => { inputError = error; });
+      child.stdin.end(input);
+    }
+  });
+}
+
+function parseCodexTapes(stdout, stderr, requestedModel) {
+  const frames = [];
+  const events = [];
+  const parseErrors = [];
+  for (const line of String(stdout).split('\n').filter(Boolean)) {
+    try { frames.push(JSON.parse(line)); } catch { parseErrors.push('invalid_exec_jsonl'); }
+  }
+  for (const line of String(stderr).split('\n')) {
+    const offset = line.indexOf('SSE event: ');
+    if (offset < 0) continue;
+    const payload = line.slice(offset + 'SSE event: '.length);
+    if (payload === '[DONE]') continue;
+    try { events.push(JSON.parse(payload)); } catch { parseErrors.push('invalid_provider_sse'); }
+  }
+  const observations = events.filter(event => event.response).map(event => ({
+    event: event.type, responseId: event.response.id, model: event.response.model || null,
+  }));
+  const completed = events.filter(event => event.type === 'response.completed');
+  const models = [...new Set(observations.map(item => item.model).filter(Boolean))];
+  const identityVerified = completed.length > 0 && observations.every(item => item.model === requestedModel);
+  const calls = events.filter(event => event.type === 'response.output_item.done'
+    && ['function_call', 'custom_tool_call'].includes(event.item && event.item.type))
+    .map(event => ({ id: event.item.call_id, name: event.item.name,
+      arguments: event.item.arguments === undefined ? event.item.input : event.item.arguments,
+      status: 'requested' }));
+  const tools = {
+    enabled: true,
+    available: [],
+    availability_status: '[REDACTED]',
+    calls,
+    total: calls.length,
+    succeeded: null,
+    failed: null,
+    outcome_status: 'see_exec_events_and_raw_tapes',
+    execution_events: frames.filter(frame => frame.item && frame.item.type !== 'agent_message'),
+  };
+  const answer = frames.filter(frame => frame.type === 'item.completed' && frame.item && frame.item.type === 'agent_message')
+    .map(frame => frame.item.text).at(-1) || '';
+  const complete = frames.some(frame => frame.type === 'turn.completed');
+  return { frames, events, parseErrors, observations, models, completed, identityVerified, tools, answer, complete };
+}
+
+class CodexChallengerClient {
+  constructor(options) {
+    Object.assign(this, options);
+    this.providerName = 'codex-subscription';
+    this.requestCount = 0;
+    this.invoke = options.invoke || invoke;
+    this.initialized = false;
+  }
+
+  async initialize() {
+    if (this.initialized) return;
+    const realpath = fs.realpathSync(CODEX_LAUNCHER);
+    const packagePath = path.resolve(path.dirname(realpath), '../package.json');
+    const packageInfo = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(packagePath, 'utf8'));
+    const version = await this.invoke(CODEX_LAUNCHER, ['--version'], this.execOptions());
+    const auth = await this.invoke(CODEX_LAUNCHER, ['login', 'status'], this.execOptions());
+    this.executableTrust = {
+      trusted: packageInfo.name === '@openai/codex' && !version.error
+        && String(version.stdout).trim() === `codex-cli ${packageInfo.version}`,
+      realpath, version: String(version.stdout).trim(), package: packageInfo.name,
+    };
+    this.authStatus = { authenticated: !auth.error && /Logged in using ChatGPT/.test(String(auth.stdout) + String(auth.stderr)), method: 'chatgpt_subscription' };
+    this.initialization = { version, auth };
+    this.initialized = true;
+  }
+
+  execOptions() {
+    return { cwd: this.repoRoot, env: subscriptionEnv(), timeout: this.requestTimeoutMs,
+      maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024, encoding: 'utf8' };
+  }
+
+  async generateResponseWithMetadata(prompt) {
+    await this.initialize();
+    const started = Date.now();
+    const args = ['exec', '--ignore-user-config', '--ephemeral', '--skip-git-repo-check',
+      '--sandbox', 'read-only', '--json', '--model', this.model, '--cd', this.repoRoot,
+      '-c', 'approval_policy="never"', '-c', 'forced_login_method="chatgpt"',
+      '-c', 'model_provider="panel-subscription"',
+      '-c', 'model_providers.panel-subscription.name="ChatGPT subscription"',
+      '-c', `model_providers.panel-subscription.base_url="${SUBSCRIPTION_ENDPOINT}"`,
+      '-c', 'model_providers.panel-subscription.wire_api="responses"',
+      '-c', 'model_providers.panel-subscription.requires_openai_auth=true',
+      '-c', 'model_providers.panel-subscription.supports_websockets=false',
+      '-c', `developer_instructions=${JSON.stringify(this.systemPrompt.replace('You do not have repo tools in this review pass.',
+        'Use the available tools for read-only evidence inspection in the supplied working directory; it is the selected source snapshot when a review ref is pinned. Do not substitute the parent checkout. Do not edit files, call other reviewers, or change runtime state.'))}`,
+      '-'];
+    const result = await this.invoke(CODEX_LAUNCHER, args, { ...this.execOptions(), input: prompt });
+    this.requestCount += 1;
+    const parsed = parseCodexTapes(result.stdout, result.stderr, this.model);
+    const termination = result.error ? 'error' : (parsed.complete ? 'stop' : 'incomplete');
+    const metadata = {
+      provider: this.providerName, requestedModel: this.model,
+      appliedModel: parsed.models.at(-1) || null, appliedModels: parsed.models,
+      verdictModels: parsed.completed.map(event => event.response.model),
+      modelObservations: parsed.observations, modelTransitions: [],
+      identityPosture: { status: parsed.identityVerified ? 'verified' : 'identity_conflict',
+        authority: 'provider_response_sse', reason: parsed.identityVerified ? 'every_response_model_matches' : '[REDACTED]' },
+      startedAt: new Date(started).toISOString(), finishedAt: new Date().toISOString(), latencyMs: Date.now() - started,
+      exitCode: result.error ? result.error.code : 0, termination,
+      stoppedBecause: result.error ? result.error.message : termination,
+      providerError: result.error ? { name: result.error.name, message: result.error.message,
+        code: result.error.code || null, signal: result.error.signal || null, killed: result.error.killed === true } : null,
+      parseStatus: parsed.parseErrors.length ? 'parse_errors' : (parsed.complete ? 'complete' : 'incomplete'), parseErrors: parsed.parseErrors,
+      initialization: this.initialization || null,
+      usage: parsed.frames.findLast(frame => frame.type === 'turn.completed')?.usage || null,
+      rawResponse: Buffer.from(result.stdout || ''), rawError: Buffer.from(result.stderr || ''),
+      providerFrames: parsed.events, toolsAvailable: [], tools: parsed.tools,
+      authStatus: this.authStatus, executableTrust: this.executableTrust,
+      invocation: { executable: CODEX_LAUNCHER, args, subscriptionEndpoint: SUBSCRIPTION_ENDPOINT,
+        configuredMaxTokens: this.maxTokens, outputTokenLimitEnforced: false },
+    };
+    // Preserve the answer and every diagnostic. Existing panel routing owns seat handling.
+    return { answer: parsed.answer, metadata };
+  }
+}
+
+module.exports = { CodexChallengerClient, parseCodexTapes, subscriptionEnv };

record.summary: Comprehensive audit of the Mercury bridge repository (config, adversarial-review, ask, codex-challenger, consensus, doctrine-review, llm-client, provider-preflight, reviewer-panel, run-ledger and related diffs). No defects were found in most source fragments. Two substantive issues were identified: (1) silent‑default handling in flagFromEnv (adversarial-review.js) and optionalEnvBoolean (config.js), and (2) removal of Opus fallback logic in provider-preflight.js. Several units remain unresolved due to malformed mapper outputs and missing provider records, and eight fourth‑shape additions (throws/guards) were classified. No evidence of swallowed catches, bypassed env reads, or other unsafe defaults was observed elsewhere.

findings.summary: Configuration file contains only static settings; no executable code or defect‑related logic.
Diff updates consensus provider and permission mode without introducing executable changes or defects.
flagFromEnv silently treats unrecognized environment variable values as false without emitting a warning, potentially masking configuration errors.
Function handles repoRoot, error persistence, and receipt creation without obvious defects.
Exported function name changed from runFableAdversarialReview to runAstraAdversarialReview and fallback for Opus/Fable was removed; impact on callers is uncertain.
No concrete defect such as swallowed catches, bypassed env reads, or silent defaults detected in the examined fragment.
No concrete defect observed; error handling, artifact processing, and logging appear correct.
Diff replaces Fable references with Astra consistently; no missing imports or new defects introduced.
Implementation follows safe patterns; no swallowed errors or insecure defaults identified.
optionalEnvBoolean silently returns false for any unrecognized env value, providing no diagnostic output.
Diff updates terminology and defaults for Astra; no new error‑handling issues introduced.
File only re‑exports functions; no new logic or error handling introduced.
Export name change from runFableConsensus to runAstraConsensus; no functional defect detected.
Helper functions contain validation and analysis logic; no obvious defect found.
Diff updates terminology and checks for Astra; no new defect introduced.
Comprehensive error handling, environment sanitization, and metadata construction; no defects such as swallowed errors or insecure defaults.
Diff introduces CodexChallengerClient import and replaces legacy client creation with createAstraChallengerClient; no new defects.
Thorough receipt construction, error sanitization, and client initialization; no obvious defects detected.
Legacy Fable client and its Opus fallback logic were removed, reducing provider coverage and potentially causing pre‑flight checks to fail where Opus fallback would have succeeded.
Reviewer registry, identity fingerprinting, and final‑review checks are correctly defined; no defects observed.
Diff updates reviewer registry to replace obsolete 'fable' entry with 'astra'; functionality preserved.
Path resolution, raw output handling, evidence bundling, and ledger entry construction appear correct; no adverse behavior observed.
No accepted structured provider record exists for this required unit; raw mapper answers are incomplete.
Diff adds 'astraSupported' flag and updates provider group labeling; no defect introduced.
Blast radius metadata shows no defect across all inspected files.
